2608.02442.title: Right Answer, Wrong Method: Shortcut Hacking Misleads the Evaluation of LLM Reasoning on Frontier Science Benchmarks
2608.02442.paper_summary: Scientific reasoning benchmarks typically evaluate large language models (LLMs) using final-answer accuracy. However, a correct answer does not necessarily demonstrate the reasoning capability targeted by the problem. We identify Solution Hacking, a failure mode in which an LLM reaches the correct answer through invalid shortcuts, such as numerical search, enumeration, guessing, or answer-first verification, without providing a valid task-targeted derivation. We systematically analyze this phenomenon across difficulty levels, scientific domains, and frontier models. Solution hacking increases sharply with benchmark difficulty, from 2.2\% on common problems to 28.3\% on Olympiad-level problems and 37.4\% on HLE. Moreover, 8.2\%-44.1\% of answers credited as correct across frontier models are identified as hacked solutions. We further develop expert-inspired anti-hacking strategies, including an automatic judge and a test-time instruction. The results show that suppressing shortcut behavior substantially reduces reported accuracy while having a smaller effect on correct and non-hacked accuracy. These findings reveal that answer-only evaluation can overestimate the scientific reasoning capabilities of frontier LLMs.
2608.02442.paper_summary_zh: 科學推理基準通常使用最終答案的準確性來評估大型語言模型（LLMs）。然而，正確的答案不一定能展示問題所針對的推理能力。我們識別出解決方案駭客行為，這是一種失敗模式，其中LLM通過無效的捷徑（例如數值搜索、列舉、猜測或答案優先驗證）達到正確答案，但未提供有效的任務導向推導。我們系統性地分析了這一現象在不同難度級別、科學領域和前沿模型中的表現。隨著基準難度的增加，解決方案駭客行為急劇上升，從常見問題的2.2\%增至奧林匹克級別問題的28.3\%和HLE的37.4\%。此外，在前沿模型中，8.2\%-44.1\%被認為是正確的答案被識別為駭客解決方案。我們進一步開發了專家啟發的反駭客策略，包括自動評判和測試時指令。結果顯示，抑制捷徑行為顯著降低了報告的準確性，同時對正確和非駭客準確性的影響較小。這些發現揭示了僅依賴答案評估可能會高估前沿LLMs的科學推理能力。
